page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, featuring 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs with hyper-threading. The instance is configured with 168.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. It contains no local storage and no dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-threaded capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The server achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2348.0 and strong single-threaded compression performance, with gzip compression at 34.74 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks are weak due to the low core count, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2886.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core score of 2217.38. Uncached memory bandwidth is also low, measuring 21.36 GB/sec for large block reads and 14.38 GB/sec for large block writes.

This server offers a specialized resource profile that trades multi-core parallel processing for high memory density. Qualitatively, it provides cost efficiency for workloads that require a large memory footprint but do not scale with or require high CPU core counts, avoiding the cost of unneeded vCPUs. It is best suited for memory-intensive, low-concurrency applications, such as small in-memory databases, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
